rows.text:
Ines Okafor arrived on Harrow Quay as the new keeper of the Salt Ledger, the only passenger on the ferry. Ines Okafor was sent to take up the post of Keeper of the Salt Ledger on Harrow Quay.

Ines found the Salt Ledger's pages for February to June gone, leaving only a row of torn stubs in the book.

Mara Venn left Ines alone with the lamp in the archive and went down the stairs without another word. Did Aldous Brandt take the missing spring pages of the Salt Ledger with him when he left Harrow Quay?

rows.text:
Ines Okafor arrived on Harrow Quay as the new keeper of the Salt Ledger, the only passenger on the ferry. Aldous Brandt was the former keeper of the Salt Ledger for thirty years, and he had been gone for three weeks. Ines Okafor set out in the morning to find anyone who had worked with Aldous Brandt.

Tobiah Wren said he did not carry Aldous Brandt off the island, contradicting the printed account that Brandt had simply left. Tobiah Wren left Ines Okafor on the quay and sailed north to the cod banks, not returning before the equinox. Ines Okafor noticed a locked brass tide-clock set into the wall on the landing below the archive. Anselm Pike brought Ines Okafor soup and told her he had played chess with Aldous Brandt every Thursday for eleven years. An unsigned note was pushed under the archive door, saying the spring pages were not burned, and Ines Okafor locked it in her trunk. Ines Okafor found that twenty-four barrels of salt a month had come onto the island but never reached the ledger.

Ines Okafor dropped the pasted handbill in the stove and went on working. Who is moving the unrecorded salt onto Harrow Quay unseen, and who is buying the fish it cures?

rows.text:
Ines Okafor arrived on Harrow Quay as the new keeper of the Salt Ledger, the only passenger on the ferry. Aldous Brandt was the former keeper of the Salt Ledger for thirty years, and he had been gone for three weeks. Ines Okafor planned to carry her salt tally to the council in the morning.

Tobiah Wren said he did not carry Aldous Brandt off the island, contradicting the printed account that Brandt had simply left. Ines Okafor noticed a locked brass tide-clock set into the wall on the landing below the archive. An unsigned note was pushed under the archive door, saying the spring pages were not burned, and Ines Okafor locked it in her trunk. That night a second note signed by the Cormorant was pushed under the archive door. The unseen visitor took Ines Okafor's salt tally from the desk, while the ledger and the biscuit tin of receipts were left untouched. Dr Pike offered to keep the receipts in a strongbox in his dispensary, and Ines Okafor was asked to hand them over.

At the tower steps, Dr Pike's offer to hold the receipts tin in his strongbox was a kind and sensible one. Will Ines Okafor hand her receipts tin over to Dr Pike, and will the tin then be safe?

rows.text:
Ines Okafor arrived on Harrow Quay as the new keeper of the Salt Ledger, the only passenger on the ferry. Aldous Brandt was the former keeper of the Salt Ledger for thirty years, and he had been gone for three weeks. Mara Venn is the harbourmaster, who led Ines Okafor to the archive and asked for the Salt Ledger audit to be finished. Ines Okafor planned to carry her salt tally to the council in the morning.

Tobiah Wren said he did not carry Aldous Brandt off the island, contradicting the printed account that Brandt had simply left. Tobiah Wren left Ines Okafor on the quay and sailed north to the cod banks, not returning before the equinox. Ines Okafor found the spring pages of the Salt Ledger torn out, and Mara Venn said the book was found that way the morning Brandt was gone. Anselm Pike brought Ines Okafor soup and told her he had played chess with Aldous Brandt every Thursday for eleven years. Mara Lisle said that in his last month Aldous Brandt stopped sleeping, went to the salt warehouse at night, and returned with chalk on his sleeves. An unsigned note was pushed under the archive door, saying the spring pages were not burned, and Ines Okafor locked it in her trunk. Ines Okafor counted salt over four days and found that 24 barrels a month arrived on the island without reaching the ledger. Mara Venn refused to open the salt warehouse without a council order, saying it was sealed until the market. Ines Okafor copied her salt count onto one sheet, showing forty barrels in the book against sixty-four on the receipts, month by month. Someone climbed the tower stairs just before midnight, passed the landing, and entered the archive after the lamp went out. The unseen visitor took Ines Okafor's salt tally from the desk, while the ledger and the biscuit tin of receipts were left untouched. At first light Ines Okafor searched the archive again for her missing salt tally, but it was not there.

Anselm Pike urged Ines Okafor to hand over the receipts tin that night, before it went the way of her tally. Anselm Pike offered to keep the receipts in a strongbox in his dispensary, where he said nobody searches. Will Ines Okafor trust Anselm Pike with the receipts tin and his strongbox, or keep the receipts herself?
